claim: Joe Biden said “You know, we have to come together. That’s why I’m running. I’m running as a proud Democrat for the Senate. So vote! Vote!”

sub_claims.question: Did Joe Biden say the phrase 'I'm running as a proud Democrat for the Senate' in 2020?
sub_claims.answer: Yes, Joe Biden made a verbal gaffe in October 2020 during a campaign event where he mistakenly said he was running for the Senate instead of President.

evidence.statement: Joe Biden made a verbal gaffe at a campaign rally in Toledo, Ohio on October 12, 2020, in which he mistakenly said 'I'm running as a proud Democrat for the Senate' instead of referring to the presidency, an incident widely covered by major news outlets including Fox News and The New York Post.

sub_claims.question: Was the full quote 'You know, we have to come together. That’s why I’m running. I’m running as a proud Democrat for the Senate. So vote! Vote!' accurately reported?
sub_claims.answer: The core part about running for the Senate is accurate from the gaffe, but the exact wording of the entire quote may not be verbatim or complete.

evidence.statement: Multiple news organizations and video recordings captured Biden saying the phrase 'I'm running as a proud Democrat for the Senate' during the October 12, 2020 Toledo event, though the precise wording of the broader surrounding remarks varied across different reported versions of the speech.

sub_claims.question: Did Joe Biden make this statement on December 10, 2020?
sub_claims.answer: No, the incident occurred in October 2020. By December 10, 2020, Biden was President-elect and not campaigning for any office.

evidence.statement: Joe Biden's gaffe occurred on October 12, 2020, at a campaign event in Toledo, Ohio, and Biden was declared President-elect on November 7, 2020, after winning the November 3, 2020 presidential election.

sub_claims.question: Was Joe Biden running for the U.S. Senate in the 2020 election?
sub_claims.answer: No, Joe Biden was the Democratic nominee for President in the 2020 election, not for the Senate.

evidence.statement: Joe Biden was the Democratic nominee for President of the United States in the 2020 election, having formally accepted the nomination at the virtual Democratic National Convention in August 2020; Biden had previously served as U.S. Senator from Delaware from 1973 to 2009 but was not running for any Senate seat in 2020.
